I think the major difference between this "tool" and the past "tools" is that AI is going to replace left brained thinking for most jobs. It is already better at the "execution layer" in the digital world than humans - only reason most people haven't seen it yet is the lack of infrastructure and scaffolding for it. What it has done to the software engineering (relegating engineers to operations leads) is a precursor to what it will do in the rest of the knowledge economy - then it will handle the operations too. In many domains, the only thing left will be the purely human to human relational and accountability pieces - and only when the human is better at the relational than the AI - which is not a given. It is already a better writer than most people. And this execution automation will permeate to the physical world too with robots. It might not take your job, but it will automate the operations, engineering, planning, management --> basically the left brained thinking. The problem is that only the rare exceptional engineers, thinkers, communicators, and connectors will be hirable in a lot of fields - the rare people who are better than its training distribution and who can pivot and think creatively where it can't. The other places where AI doesn't replace us will almost be more manufactured decisions by us given the fact that we are still in charge - places where we decide we want a human there just because... e.g. childcare, lawyers, government officials, etc... not necessarily because the AI 'couldn't' to the job. There is a lot we need to figure out and prepare for.
